references.title: Winter lamp with wreath
references.lesson: A dish shade, transparent round light and green life ring create a readable seasonal lamp with seven parts.
references.placement_notes: The thin post has no pavement footing. Design its support before installation, and keep the wreath clear of pedestrians and nearby walls. Connection analysis leaves 3 optimistic groups; inspect those unresolved interfaces during adaptation.

visual_review.note: Home and front show a slender black stem, a clear yellow light and a green ring with a red accent. The open ring gives detail without a bulky body.

references.title: Ornamental globe lamp
references.lesson: An inverted transparent globe and a sideways foliage sprig give a street fitting a distinctive silhouette.
references.placement_notes: Reserve the round four-stud base and the asymmetric foliage envelope. Check the bar, globe and sprig interfaces when adapting its height. Connection analysis leaves 9 optimistic groups; inspect those unresolved interfaces during adaptation.

visual_review.note: Home and front show a white and grey round base, a narrow post, transparent globe and offset green sprig with red and white berries.

references.title: Small ornamental tree
references.lesson: Stacked brown cones and differently angled foliage produce a tapered trunk and a compact organic crown.
references.placement_notes: Treat this as a narrow ornamental plant or a small tree at the chosen scene scale. Add a ground attachment; the source does not include a landscape base. Connection analysis leaves 7 optimistic groups; inspect those unresolved interfaces during adaptation.

visual_review.note: Home and front show three overlapping leaf shapes above a tapering brown trunk. Its small crown would not read as a large shade tree.

references.title: Layered woodland tree
references.lesson: Round trunk courses and rotated foliage layers create a broad canopy with irregular edges.
references.placement_notes: The green base is four studs square, but foliage spreads about 11.6 studs. Reserve that canopy envelope and adjust layer angles instead of simply scaling the source. Connection analysis leaves 5 optimistic groups; inspect those unresolved interfaces during adaptation.

visual_review.note: Home and front show three distinct canopy levels with open space between them. The brown vertical trunk remains legible through the branches.

references.title: Moulded staircase and landing
references.lesson: A dedicated staircase provides thin risers and an open underside with far fewer parts than stacked solid bricks.
references.placement_notes: Reserve four studs across the stair and a twelve-stud source depth including the narrow upper landing. Match the actual landing height to the floor; add handrails where the brief needs them.

visual_review.note: Home and top show open brown treads and a narrower two-stud landing extension. Both ends need integration with the surrounding floors.

references.title: Arched panel with side clips
references.lesson: A small arch, grooved top edge and side clips combine a shaped opening with a useful attachment vocabulary.
references.placement_notes: This is a narrow roof-notch wall insert, not a complete dormer. Preserve the side-clip clearance and source orientation, and inspect the adjoining roof before attaching a new panel.

visual_review.note: Home and top show an arched opening, projecting upper trim and two clips on one side. The silhouette is useful as a compact roof or facade detail.

references.title: Two-track loading ramp
references.lesson: Two wheel tracks, hinge fingers and a small grille communicate a functional loading surface while keeping the centre open.
references.placement_notes: Measure the mating hinge in the host truck and match its finger spacing. Check both deployed and folded clearance; the source image shows only its stored local pose.

visual_review.note: Home and top show parallel dark tracks joined by grey crosspieces. The open centre and small red accents distinguish the ramp from a solid tailgate.

references.title: Opening window with shutters
references.lesson: Dedicated window leaves and louvred shutters add depth and a recognizable opening mechanism to a facade.
references.placement_notes: Use the frame footprint for the wall opening, not the approximately 7.5-stud open-shutter envelope. Reserve front and side sweep and preserve the leaf pivots. Connection analysis leaves 3 optimistic groups; inspect those unresolved interfaces during adaptation.

visual_review.note: Home and right show a brown frame, blue inner leaves and grey louvred shutters at different angles. The side view exposes the depth that a flat facade would miss.

references.title: Timbered wall and projecting arches
references.lesson: Patterned timber panels, a shutter and paired arches create strong architectural identity in a small wall section.
references.placement_notes: The arches project well beyond the upright wall. Preserve their roof-support relationship, inspect the source base, and adapt the red palette deliberately to the new building.

visual_review.note: Home and right show red panels with black timber markings, a yellow shutter and two tall projecting grey arches. The exposed arches need the adjoining roof context.

references.title: Airliner engine and pylon
references.lesson: A dedicated cylindrical engine casing, turbine face and exhaust create a convincing nacelle with a thin brick-built pylon.
references.placement_notes: Reserve the four-stud engine diameter and eleven-stud source length. Match the pylon top studs to the wing and check fan and exhaust clearances before repeating the module. Connection analysis leaves 7 optimistic groups; inspect those unresolved interfaces during adaptation.

visual_review.note: Home and right show a readable fan intake, silver cylinder, white tapered exhaust and swept white pylon with a blue stripe.

references.title: Sloped tail fin with beacon
references.lesson: A sequence of slopes, a thin contrasting base and a transparent tip make a small fin recognizable from a distance.
references.placement_notes: Use the six-stud long, narrow source profile as a scale reference. Side studs protrude beyond the nominal one-stud thickness; align the base to the fuselage and retain clearance.

visual_review.note: Home and right show a stepped dark fin, yellow base stripe and transparent red tip. The edge view confirms a slim profile with side-stud projections.

references.title: Tapered wing with hinge root
references.lesson: Wedge plates establish a taper while hinge fingers, a grille and a small light give the wing a clear root and tip.
references.placement_notes: The source is the left wing. Inspect the matching right assembly rather than assuming reflection preserves connectors; reserve the root hinge sweep and approximately 12.8-stud span.

visual_review.note: Home and top show a tapered yellow planform, dark root, two slim surface strips and an amber tip light. The detailing leaves most of the wing surface quiet.

references.title: Classic compact truck tractor
references.lesson: A moulded windscreen, doors, grille, lights and antenna make a compact truck read as a vehicle rather than a box.
references.placement_notes: This source includes wheels and rear chassis as well as the cab. Inspect its coupling and wheel envelope before attaching a trailer; retain or replace the branded panel deliberately. Connection analysis leaves 8 optimistic groups; inspect those unresolved interfaces during adaptation.

visual_review.note: Home and top show a white cab with blue glazing, red belt line, green grille and visible wheel clearance. The rear chassis remains open for a trailer connection.

references.title: Mini construction truck cab
references.lesson: A narrow windscreen, shaped roof, grille and small wheel assemblies convey construction-vehicle character at a compact scale.
references.placement_notes: The cab body is only two studs wide with tyres extending beyond it. Use its actual dimensions instead of assuming minifigure seating, and build the rear body around the exposed chassis.

visual_review.note: Home and top show a compact yellow cab, dark glazing, sloped shoulders and four tyres. It offers a visibly different scale and silhouette from the classic truck.

references.title: Spacecraft wheel module
references.lesson: Wheel-pin plates, a tall bracket and small exhaust and grille fittings give a compact wheeled module a mechanical identity.
references.placement_notes: The original parent calls this landing gear; its isolated appearance also suggests rover ideas. Preserve the hinge and bracket interfaces and test deployed clearance in the parent before reuse. Connection analysis leaves 7 optimistic groups; inspect those unresolved interfaces during adaptation.

visual_review.note: Home and top show four wide tyres, a raised bracket, orange slopes and paired exhaust openings. The structural bracket gives useful height without filling the centre with bricks.

references.title: Airliner wheel bogie
references.lesson: Small wheel carriers and a compact upright mounting pair create aircraft landing gear with a clear silhouette.
references.placement_notes: This System aircraft fitting contains a few Technic connector pieces. Match the upper mounting interface and tyre ground plane to the host aircraft; this is not a retracting mechanism recipe. Connection analysis leaves 5 optimistic groups; inspect those unresolved interfaces during adaptation.

visual_review.note: Home and right show two wheel stations under a flat deck and a short upright mounting pair. The open space around the wheels keeps the module visually light.

references.title: Faceted research-ship bow
references.lesson: Side-stud bricks and small slopes shape a compact ship bow in multiple directions without scaling any physical part.
references.placement_notes: The source axes do not present the bow as a complete horizontal hull. Consult the parent placement matrix before orienting it, and continue its red, dark blue and grey bands into the adjoining hull. Connection analysis leaves 3 optimistic groups; inspect those unresolved interfaces during adaptation.

visual_review.note: Home and right show smooth dark blue sloping surfaces over red stepped shoulders and a narrow grey edge. This is an isolated bow segment, not a finished boat.

references.title: Rounded cockpit shell
references.lesson: Repeated curved roof pieces form a smooth shell while narrow side ledges leave space for a cockpit or nose insert.
references.placement_notes: The source shell is six studs wide and open at one end and underneath. Preserve the ledges and rear opening, then build the glazing, floor and host attachments for the new model.

visual_review.note: Home and right show a white rounded rear shell and two long open rails. The continuous curved roof is useful bodywork inspiration but the module is visibly incomplete on its own.

references.title: Fire-escape railing insert
references.lesson: Bars and articulated small elements produce thin open ironwork that reads more delicately than stacked wall bricks.
references.placement_notes: This is a railing insert and support strip from a larger fire escape, not a complete stair. Preserve the angled bar connections and locate the strip in its floor or balcony context.

visual_review.note: Home and right show a narrow grey support strip with dark open ironwork at one end. Angled upright elements give the railing a distinctive industrial rhythm.

references.title: Classical arch and cornice
references.lesson: A moulded arch, grooved masonry and round plates under the cornice create shadow lines in a shallow facade bay.
references.placement_notes: The source is only one stud deep and has two separate pier feet. Tie both piers into the host base and continue the cornice rhythm; use the parameterized arcade recipe for another height.

visual_review.note: Home and right show a tan arch, fine horizontal grooves and a row of round spacers below the upper beam. The thin depth is useful for economical facade relief.

references.title: Park bench with shaped back
references.lesson: Dedicated shaped back elements and a mostly tiled seat create a recognizable bench with a low part count.
references.placement_notes: Reserve eight studs of width and the backrest overhang beyond the two-stud seat. Attach the two white feet to the pavement and keep the seat studs accessible if adding figures.

visual_review.note: Home and right show a dark blue seat and reclined rounded back above short white feet. Smooth seat edges contrast with the few exposed mounting studs.

references.title: Two-axle train bogie with buffers and magnetic coupling
references.lesson: Combine two wheelsets, a bogie pivot and a coupling on one supported undercarriage; minifigure heads become buffer faces.
references.placement_notes: The locomotive chassis and receiving mount for the bogie pin. The parent turns this assembly 90 degrees about Y and places it at [-170, 56, 0]. It does not provide a motor or powered transmission for this bogie. Keep the wheelsets, pin and coupling stack together. Reserve turning space around the bogie and buffer faces; do not assume clearance on a different chassis or track curve.

visual_review.note: Home and the context/right-view board show both wheelsets, the central mounting pin, magnetic coupling and paired round buffer faces.

references.construction: Two 2878c02 wheelsets sit at local Z = -60 and +60. The 4092b short-pin bogie plate supplies the upward pivot. The buffer beam, coupling and magnet are included.
references.description_check: The database says single-axle; the section actually contains two single-axle wheelset assemblies, making a two-axle bogie.

discovery.description: Rear wheel bogie — single-axle train wheelset, minifig-head buffers, buffer beam, magnetic coupling, coupler and bogie plate
discovery.parent_description: Red and dark-red diesel switcher locomotive on a 6x28 train base: grille-vented sides with hinged body panels, glazed cab with windscreen and opening train doors, double-curved dark-bluish-grey roof, headlight and tail-light round plates, interior minifig seat and turntable, underside underframe detail, and two magnetic-coupled single-axle wheel bogies

references.title: Balcony facade with door, dormer and planted railing
references.lesson: Integrate a balcony floor, door threshold, decorative railing and sloped roof window into a layered facade module.
references.placement_notes: The building below, side/rear enclosure and surrounding roof. The complete-model parent places this section at [78, -185, 120], rotated 180 degrees about Y. Its plate underside needs support across the host building. Preserve the door opening and plate support grid. Rebuild wall courses when changing width; do not stretch the roof window, fencing or glazing.

visual_review.note: Home and the context/right-view board show the projecting balcony, sloping dormer glazing, wall and door. The side view exposes the thin wall and floor that need the parent building.

references.construction: A tan plate floor carries a turquoise wall with door and glazing. Dark-blue slopes frame a dedicated 60806 roof window; fences and brown trim form the balcony edge.
references.description_check: The description is broadly accurate, but this is a facade/floor fragment, not a complete room or self-supporting building.

discovery.description: First-floor balcony - turquoise brick railing with dark-blue slopes forming a dormered bay, a white roof-window, brown door and trim, plus small floral accents on a tan/white plate base.
discovery.parent_description: Complete Bookshop diorama - a two-building street scene featuring a tan/turquoise bookshop with dormer windows and a dark-red mansard roof, a neighbouring white/turquoise townhouse with a bay window and balcony, plus an ornamental tree, lampposts, a pendulum clock, bookshelves, and two minifigures.

references.title: Compact aircraft landing strut with matched wheel and tyre
references.lesson: Use a short axle and two angle connectors to separate the fuselage mounting pin from a freely mounted wheel.
references.placement_notes: The fuselage Technic receiving bricks and the placement angle. The parent contains two differently rotated occurrences at X = -50 and +50; the extracted strut is not already in its installed orientation. Keep the wheel/tyre pair and pin roles. Measure the host receiving hole before placement and review the complete fuselage clearance. Six optimistic connection groups remain for seven placements: this is a geometry study, not a verified mechanical core.

visual_review.note: Home and the context/right-view board show the wheel, two-connector strut and separate mounting pin, with both installed occurrences visible through the ghosted aircraft.

references.construction: Two 32013 angle connectors are joined by a 32062 axle. A 2780 friction pin supplies the host attachment, while a 3673 pin carries the 42610 rim and 51011 tyre.
references.description_check: The description calls it retractable. The source shows one pose only; retraction travel, locking and wheel clearance have not been demonstrated.

discovery.description: Retractable main landing gear strut using Technic angle connectors, an axle, and pins to mount a rubber tyred wheel.
discovery.parent_description: Complete Harrier Jet model combining a fuselage, cockpit, swept wings with hardpoints, twin vertical tail, exhaust nozzles, and retractable landing gear into a VTOL fighter aircraft.

references.title: Hinged spacecraft side hatch with bracket-mounted engine cone
references.lesson: Carry an engine cone, fin and layered side shell on a hinged module while leaving the mating hinge half in the hull.
references.placement_notes: The mating 3830 hinge top: the hull places it at [-60, -128, 240], beside the hatch occurrence at [-60, -72, 240]. The opposite hatch is a separately authored section, not permission to reflect rigid parts. Copy or rebuild the hull-side hinge support before claiming an attached hatch. Preserve hinge alignment and reserve the swept space; opening travel is not checked by this static source.

visual_review.note: Home and the context/right-view board show the exposed hinge fingers, sideways cone, fin and layered hatch positioned at the rear of the spacecraft.

references.construction: A 3831 hinge base is bonded into plates and inverted slopes. A 3956 bracket presents a perpendicular attachment for the 3943b cone. The fin and cap complete the side silhouette.
references.description_check: The description identifies the visible elements correctly but omits the critical mating hinge half in the parent.

discovery.description: A blue left-side hatch assembly mirroring the right, with inverted slopes, a hinge base, bracket, tail fin, and a light grey engine cone.
discovery.parent_description: A classic LEGO Space Cruiser composed of a grey-winged spaceship, two blue hinged side hatches, a trans-yellow cockpit canopy, a wheeled grey forklift with a white container, and two Classic Space minifigures (red and white).

references.title: Small warehouse forklift with dedicated lifting mast
references.lesson: Build a complete small service vehicle around a dedicated mast rather than inventing a lifting linkage from loose parts.
references.placement_notes: Cargo, a cart, the aircraft and minifigures are separate scene objects. No structural part of this forklift is supplied by the parent. Its inherited body colour is red (4); the isolated xray board uses its default yellow for inherited colour. Preserve the mast and matched wheel/tyre pairs. Change surrounding bodywork and palette, then check ground contact and fork clearance. Cargo fit, load stability and lift travel remain unverified.

visual_review.note: The red home preview and context/right-view board show four wheels, tall mast, raised forks and operator controls. The ghosted parent confirms this is a separate vehicle, not a disconnected component of the airplane.

references.construction: Wheel-pin plates support four wheels, with larger tyres beside the mast. The 3430c01 shortcut includes the mast and raised black forks; two controls and a handle complete the operator area.
references.description_check: The database description is broadly accurate. The lifting function belongs to a dedicated complete-part shortcut; the MPD represents its raised pose, not an actuated mechanism.

discovery.description: A small forklift vehicle with wheels, a forklift mast, and a control stick for lifting cargo.
discovery.parent_description: An airport service set featuring an airplane, a forklift, a cargo cart, a shipping case, and two minifigure characters.

references.title: Seven-part swivel armchair with sideways tiled armrests
references.lesson: Turn a moulded seat into a compact armchair using opposing brackets, sideways tiles and a complete turntable pair.
references.placement_notes: Only the room/floor context; both turntable halves are included. The source places the chair at an angle through a proper Y rotation, rather than changing its internal construction. Keep the bracket offsets and turntable pair. Recolour or place the whole chair, leaving room around its armrests; verify floor attachment separately when mounting it.

visual_review.note: Home and the context/right-view board show a complete seat with two smooth vertical armrests in a furnished room. The single optimistic connection group supports selection, not physical certification.

references.construction: A 3680 base and 3679 turntable top support two opposing 99207 brackets, a 4079 seat and two vertical 3068b armrest tiles.
references.description_check: The short description is accurate but undersells the construction: the two brackets and vertical tiles form the armrests, and the turntable includes both halves.

discovery.description: A small black armchair built on a turntable base with brackets and a minifig seat.
discovery.parent_description: Assorted accessories including suitcases, a crowbar, and decorative dishes for the hotel lobby display.
